anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the INA219 (U1) has SCL/SDA (pins 5/6) on I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC with A0/A1 (pins 7/8) tied to GND, and the sheet note reads 'I2C address: 0x40'. On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685 (U2) has SCL/SDA (pins 26/27) on the SAME nets I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC, with all six address pins A0-A5 (1,2,3,4,5,24) tied to GND, i.e. also 0x40. The two 0x40 devices therefore sit on one I2C bus together with the FCC EEPROM (U3, 0x50).
anomalies.expected: Two slaves cannot share an I2C bus with identical 7-bit addresses. The spec lists both as 0x40 ('NXP PCA9685PW ... I2C addr 0x40' and 'TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40'), which only works if they are on separate buses; the schematic even annotates the PCA9685 block with 'I2C address: 0x41' (A0 high) and leaves I2C1/I2C3 free, indicating the PWM driver was meant not to clash with the INA219 on I2C2.

FCC Peripherals sheet, U2 PCA9685PW: pin26 -> I2C2_SCL_FCC, pin27 -> I2C2_SDA_FCC, A0-A5 tied to GND, note 'I2C address: 0x41'

anomalies.impact: Bus contention on I2C2: the FCC MCU cannot reliably address one of the two 0x40 slaves, so servo PWM output and/or battery current/voltage telemetry will fail or be corrupted.

anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685 EXTCLK pin (25) is tied directly to GND, while OE (23) is also tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: Standard practice (and the PCA9685 datasheet) requires EXTCLK to be left floating when the internal oscillator is used; driving it low makes the chip expect an external clock at 0 Hz and stops the internal oscillator, so no PWM is generated. The spec is silent on this pin, so it is judged by practice.

anomalies.impact: The PCA9685 internal oscillator may not run, leaving the 16 servo PWM outputs inactive.
